topic: The first Olympic Winter Games were held at Chamonix, France, 25 January–5 February 1924, at the foot of Mont Blanc. Staged as an 'International Winter Sports Week' attached to the Paris 1924 Games, they were retroactively designated the first Winter Olympics by the IOC in 1926 (olympics.com; Britannica). 16 nations and 258 athletes (247 men, 11 women) competed in 16 events (olympics.com). Norway topped the medal table with 17 medals (4 gold), Finland took 11 (4 gold); the host France won 3 medals, all bronze (Wikipedia 1924 Winter Olympics medal table; olympics.com). The second Winter Games were at St. Moritz, Switzerland, in 1928.
